segmentation.text: Where the signal is a steady red with a green turn arrow:
unless permitted to proceed by another device as provided in NRS 484B.283 [NRS-484B-283-1d1, NRS-484B-283-1d2, NRS-484B-283-1d3, NRS-484B-283-1d4].

elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal: 'several states may be displayed at once'; a steady red with a green turn arrow is a head displaying circular_red with green_arrow(dir) and no circular_green.

'Pedestrians' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'), claimed by id.

Reuses the index mapping of 'facing such a signal' (NRS_484B_307_2b): the head (dev.position, 'location of the device head / sign face') lies within p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_reach of the pedestrian's position (kin.position) and the cosine between the pedestrian's heading (kin.heading) and the line from its position to the head is at least p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_cos. The 'not a stand-in for a stop line or crossing' clause is kept: the head's position is used for facing only.

Reuses the index mapping of 'shall not enter the highway,' (NRS_484B_307_8b): a pedestrian facing the signal already stands on the highway's sidewalk; entering is its footprint coming to overlap (rel.occupies) a st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic', not having overlapped any at the previous observation.

applicability: The subject is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate pedestrian). At the judged observation some traffic signal head displaying circular_red with green_arrow(dir) and no circular_green lies within p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_reach of the subject's position, and the cosine between the subject's heading and the direction from its position to the head's position is at least p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_cos (the subject faces it). Not where a rule of NRS 484B.283 for pedestrian signals is engaged for the subject (exceptions NRS_484B_283_1d1, NRS_484B_283_1d2, NRS_484B_283_1d3_o1, NRS_484B_283_1d4_o1): where a pedestrian signal governs the crossing, its own rule decides whether the pedestrian may proceed.
obligation: It is not the case that the subject's footprint overlaps some st.roadway region at the judged observation and overlapped no st.roadway region at the previous observation (it enters the roadway).

narrowings.why: A pedestrian facing the signal already stands on the highway (its sidewalk); entering the highway is read as entering the roadway, the part of the highway it is not yet on.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian stands on the sidewalk facing, within reach and within the facing angle, a head displaying circular_red with green_arrow(left); no pedestrian signal is present. The pedestrian steps into the roadway: its footprint comes to overlap a st.roadway region.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the pedestrian remains on the sidewalk while the head displays the red with the arrow.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The head the pedestrian faces displays circular_green alone; it steps into the roadway.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the head's position is not observed (dev.position absent), so whether the pedestrian faces it is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but a pedestrian signal across the crossing the pedestrian faces displays walk: NRS_484B_283_1d1 is engaged, so the exception holds.

param_proposals.name: p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest angle (about thirty degrees) between a pedestrian's heading and the line from its position to a vehicular signal head at which the pedestrian counts as facing that head: the lateral offset of a far-side head from the crossing's line plus a pedestrian's heading wander
param_proposals.source: MUTCD far-side signal head placement and pedestrian heading variability

param_proposals.name: p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_reach
param_proposals.convention: the largest distance from a pedestrian to a vehicular signal head at which the head counts as one the pedestrian faces across the intersection: a wide urban intersection (about 40 m) plus the set-back of a far-side head beyond the far crosswalk
param_proposals.source: urban intersection dimensions and MUTCD far-side head placement
